_comment: Slakh2100 validation split, pre-encoded with the streamgen accompaniment control. Same mechanism as local_babyslakh_streamgen.json, on the full corpus with the official Slakh splits, which is what 1.2 needs to say anything about generalization. Pass --sample_size on the CLI, never as a key here: pre_encode_dataset.py's merge_config_into_args treats any argparse default that is not None as CLI-supplied, so a 'sample_size' key would be silently ignored. As run on 2026-09-08 the sbatch scripts pass --sample_size 587853 --pad --batch_size 8, i.e. a 13.3s / 144-frame window taken from the START of every track (the pre-encode path sets random_crop=False). The alternative, if whole tracks are wanted, is --sample_size 16760832 (4092 frames, 380s, the 95th percentile track length) with --batch_size 1 and no --pad; note that the silence-fraction cutoff below means something quite different at that length. Augmentation: 'augment_variants' writes that many copies of the split, variant 0 unaugmented and the rest each rolling a time-stretch rate from 'augment_time_stretch' and a pitch shift from +/- 'augment_pitch_semitones'. Both the stretch and the pitch shift go to the drums and the accompaniment with the same values ('augment_pitch_scope': 'all'), so a variant is the whole arrangement in a new key at a new tempo; the shared rate is what keeps the two frame-aligned. Set 'augment_pitch_scope' to 'controls' to hold the drums at their original tuning while still re-keying the accompaniment. Each variant is a fresh pass, so the stochastic stem submix is re-rolled per variant too. Encode time and disk scale with the variant count. Left at 1 on purpose: the held-out split is what the model is scored on, and scoring against pitched/stretched audio measures the augmentation as much as the model. Sanity check: 'sanity_check_samples' is counted PER VARIANT and the dataloader is unshuffled, so 2 x 'augment_variants' items are decoded back to audio into <output_path>/_sanity_check — the same tracks in every variant, so the variants are A/B-able against each other. Build the page with scripts/make_listening_page.py; each variant gets its own card stating the rate and interval it was written with. Silence filtering: items whose target or accompaniment is silent over the encoded window are DROPPED, not replaced (they leave a gap in the latent ids). The default is an RMS floor of -50 dBFS; '--max_silence_fraction' adds a percentage-of-silence limit and is off by default, but the sbatch scripts pass --max_silence_fraction 0.3 -- on the 13.3s window that kept 56 of 270 validation tracks, so treat it as the dominant knob on what ends up in the split. Every sidecar JSON carries a 'levels' block (rms_dbfs, silence_fraction per stream) so a cutoff can be read off a first pass, and '_skipped.json' records what went and why. See experiments/01-streamgen-conditioning/04-silence-filtering.md.
